title: Nick Baltas on Trend Following in 2026- Signals, Structure & Strategy - Systematic Investor - Ep.282

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Nick Baltas on Trend Following in 2026- Signals, Structure & Strategy - Systematic Investor - Ep.282.docx

speakers: Neils Kostrup Larsen (host, hedge fund manager)
summary: Weekly Systematic Investor episode: Baltas and Larsen review trend following in early 2026 and 2025 dispersion across speed and universe (slow and small won the last 3-4 years but not historically). They then summarise three December 2025 papers: a consultant primer on trend, nonlinear time series momentum, and ATP's theory of trend payoff. Conclusion: do not change trend design to chase recent results.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: momentum trend and following at the end of the day it's just perhaps um an expression of uh of slow digestion of information
claims.claim: Trend and momentum exist because information is digested slowly, so a continued price move in one direction is the signal.
claims.testable: partly - conceptual explanation, signal itself is testable

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if we end up achieving to get hold of prior to the price formation happening it's almost as if we'll get the momentum before the momentum itself plays out in the prices
claims.claim: News and narrative data collected before prices fully move could give a momentum signal ahead of price-based trend signals.
claims.indicator: narrative / media information data from an aggregator vendor
claims.testable: partly - idea is early, needs narrative dataset and test

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: how important it is not to have any kind of prediction in your in your model
claims.claim: Pure trend following avoids any prediction or story and so is protected when narratives (e.g. Japan hike should lift yen) fail to show up in prices.
claims.conditions: narratives often fail to move price (Japan rate rise, yen did not strengthen)
claims.testable: partly - principle, evidenced by one anecdote

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: equity prices are not necessarily impacted too much about inflation unless inflation is rising beyond a specific threshold
claims.claim: Asset reactions to a narrative or macro theme are conditional, appearing only beyond a threshold, so exposure should be measured conditionally.
claims.testable: yes - threshold conditional regression is testable

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: signal to noise quantification is important specifically for the Vshapes
claims.claim: Quantifying signal-to-noise in a market, beyond return divided by volatility, is important for avoiding V-shaped reversals, and non-price information may help.
claims.testable: partly - proxy is return/vol, richer versions undefined

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it is kind of the seventh month in a row where we're seeing very strong conditions uh for trend
claims.claim: Trend conditions were strong for seven consecutive months into January 2026, driven by metals and equities.
claims.indicator: trend index performance; metals and equities
claims.testable: yes - CTA index data is observable

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I think the universe and the speed are probably the two most important um pillars of dispersion at least for the last year
claims.claim: Dispersion in 2025 trend programs came mainly from which markets were traded (universe breadth) and trend speed; faster and more diversified programs lagged.
claims.conditions: in 2025 only equities and precious metals trended while rates repeatedly failed
claims.testable: yes - compare speed and universe variants over 2025

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the correlations were relatively elevated anyway because to your point there were a few markets that exhibited strong trends
claims.claim: Trend programs of different speeds stayed highly correlated in 2025 because the same few markets drove gains and the same markets (rates) caused losses.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: most managers probably made all the money in only a handful of markets and other than that we had many small losses maybe one or two bigger losses
claims.claim: A year where gains come from a handful of markets with many small losses is the classic trend following payoff shape, so 2025 was typical in structure.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: gen CTA index up uh 4 and a4% very strong trend index even more so up 4.67% and the short-term traders index up 1.75%
claims.claim: In early January 2026 the SG CTA index was up about 4.4%, trend index 4.67% and short-term traders 1.75%.
claims.indicator: SG CTA, trend and short-term traders indices

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: speed will create more of a dispersion than the sizing
claims.claim: If volatilities and correlations are stable, trend lookback speed drives more performance dispersion between programs than sizing method (dynamic vs static, correlation use).
claims.conditions: assumes stable vols and correlations; not tested
claims.testable: yes - can be tested by fixing universe and varying speed vs sizing

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: for the last three years and that's exactly what I said in the in the December discussion if you were slow you would have out outperformed
claims.claim: Over the last three years slow trend speeds (around 12 months, second best 9 months) ranked best in a 25-year ranking of annual speed performance, unprecedented three years in a row.
claims.indicator: trend lookback speed from 2 to 12 month half-life
claims.conditions: driven by V-shaped reversals (SVB, dollar yen, Liberation Day) hurting fast signals
claims.testable: yes - rank speeds by annual return, 25 years

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: universe wise having been small is possibly quite dominantly the outperformer for
claims.claim: Over roughly the last four years a concentrated universe (DBMF-like) outperformed a broad 80 to 100 market universe, which Baltas had not seen before in the 25-year history.
claims.conditions: recent regime; was worst in other eras
claims.testable: yes - rank universes by annual return

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: you can broaden up a small universe by just having maybe more tenors in specific interest rate markets
claims.claim: A medium-sized universe is best built thoughtfully (e.g. a few major ex-US equity indices, more tenors in rates) instead of many currencies and few equities.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: being small or trading a small universe was the worst universe every single year for something like seven years in a row
claims.claim: Small trend universes were the worst performer each year from the tech bubble aftermath through 2009, so recent small-universe outperformance by replicators should not be extrapolated.
claims.conditions: era dependent: small universes win since 2016, lost 2002 to 2009

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: in 2022 you you conclude based on your analysis that actually being very were very quick
claims.claim: In 2022 the fastest trend speeds ranked best, the opposite of the last three years, showing the best speed flips with the regime of sustained trends versus reversals.
claims.conditions: sustained trends in commodities, rates and dollar

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: reacting to out or underperformance is is the wrong recipe
claims.claim: Changing trend design (speed, universe) in response to recent out- or under-performance is the wrong approach; discipline and trust in the process matter more.
claims.testable: partly - chasing recent winners can be tested as a meta-strategy

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it is more about that the Vshapes are the ones to have caused this dispersion rather than oh actually you should have been longer term
claims.claim: Recent dispersion came from V-shaped reversals (mean reversion beyond trend dynamics), not from longer-duration trends being better.
claims.testable: partly - reversal events identifiable ex post

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: pretty much since 2022, it's been kind of the worst sector to trade
claims.claim: After 2022 many concluded to keep trading mostly fixed income because it had been the best sector for 20 years, yet it has been the worst sector since 2022, so sector concentration on the past is risky.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: all sectors have actually been profitable
claims.claim: Over about 20 years every trend sector has been profitable but contribution rotates over time, so a full-breadth portfolio is the more intuitive design.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I see it more as an opportunity set that, you know, to the extent it's available to us, we tilt in favor or against depending on the intertemporal trend
claims.claim: Baltas favors dynamic allocation across sectors, tilting toward areas with positive trend in the sector return signal, rather than static equal weights.
claims.indicator: sector-level trend signal for risk allocation

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we wrote a paper back in 2019 as to how we think of defensive solutions and what are the different pillars
claims.claim: Defensive strategies range from reactive, high-bias, expensive tail hedges to carry-generating but not downside-protecting ones, with trend following as the intermediate component (RMS framework of first and second responders).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: Stop-loss and profit uh taking triggers
claims.claim: Trend program design differences that matter: universe, speed, diversifying non-trend signals, stop-loss and profit-taking, static vs dynamic risk allocation, and volatility targeting leverage.
claims.testable: partly - each dimension can be varied in backtest

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: 2025 was a strong strong strong year for all those concepts
claims.claim: In 2025 mean reversion, micro indicators and carry trades all did well and diversified trend, so programs that included them differed from pure trend.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: allow it to be maintained in an location at times that it's actually not performing well
claims.claim: Non-trend components help investors stay allocated to trend following during its drawdowns, which matters because investors feel losses more than gains (concave utility).
claims.testable: no - behavioural benefit hard to test

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: institutions have a variety of possibilities in terms of accessing the the style
claims.claim: Institutions can now access trend through CTAs, mutual funds, UCITS, ETFs and QIS, reflecting more mainstream demand.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: a lot of trend following allocation kind of fails mostly because of the behavior or mostly because of the kind of reaction pattern of of investors
claims.claim: Trend allocations often fail because of investor behaviour, i.e. reacting to drawdowns by cutting, not because of the strategy itself.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if there are those nonlinearities instead of us forcing them by some sort of a parametric approach let's say we know we utilize something that is called a sigmoid
claims.claim: The nonlinear time series momentum paper proposes letting the data (via a neural network) determine how past returns map to positions instead of imposing a sigmoid.
claims.indicator: past return to position transfer function
claims.testable: yes - paper replication with neural net vs sigmoid

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if it's a basis point positive, then maybe I should do a basis point allocation rather than a 1% allocation
claims.claim: Linear scaling of position by signal magnitude improves on a binary long/short signal because weak signals get small positions.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there is a point whereby I just want to
claims.claim: Beyond a certain size the signal should be capped, giving a sigmoid shape (linear near zero, flat in the extremes), because estimation noise and reversion make extreme signals less reliable.
claims.conditions: extreme signals e.g. three Sharpe-ratio units of past return

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: with two full positive and two full negative exposure you'll end up acrewing a lot of costs
claims.claim: Binary signals only win via an early start, but when a signal oscillates around zero they flip full positions and accrue large trading costs, so net of costs linear or sigmoid sizing is preferable.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the data generating process is such whereby you have this continuation of return but in the tails it ends up reverting
claims.claim: Past returns continue to predict future returns near zero but revert in the extremes, so the return-to-position map is nonlinear.
claims.indicator: past return vs future return nonparametric relation
claims.direction: flatten or reverse at extreme past returns

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the minute we depart from it it is no longer just a trend strategy
claims.claim: Keeping the sign of the signal (long if positive, short if negative) preserves a trend strategy; letting the model flip sign at extremes mixes in a reversion engine that is better run separately for allocation and attribution.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: they use a neural network to effectively um um if you like extract the way that past return translates into future return
claims.claim: The paper uses a neural network to estimate the transfer function per asset class and finds tail flattening and even reversion at extremes.
claims.indicator: neural network transfer function from past returns

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: whether this incremental complexity will bring significant value versus having a sigmoid that in itself kind of be in itself behaves um in line with with with expectations
claims.claim: A neural network transfer function agrees with the sigmoid theory, so it is open whether its extra complexity adds value over a parametric sigmoid.
claims.indicator: neural network vs sigmoid trend sizing

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: even if returns are independent if volatility in itself is serally dependent you can still benefit from a trend following strategy
claims.claim: Trend following can profit even when returns are independent if volatility is serially dependent, so autocorrelation of returns is not required.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if I'm observing a significant draw down what is my expected payoff from being a trend follower
claims.claim: The ATP paper derives a trend follower's expected payoff conditional on the cumulative past return over a horizon, with a directional and a timing component.
claims.indicator: conditional payoff of binary trend signal on past cumulative return
claims.testable: yes - derive and test conditional payoff

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: beyond specific thresholds mathematically defined a trend follower can still um deliver positive return and specifically in the draw down specifically as a crisis alpha
claims.claim: Even when returns are iid, a trend follower earns positive expected payoff conditional on a deep drawdown beyond a threshold, which explains crisis alpha without serial correlation.
claims.conditions: beyond mathematically defined threshold of cumulative past return

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: how quickly can you turn into a situation whereby your um price process um is aligned in terms of direction with your signaling
claims.claim: Besides getting the average direction right (e.g. holding equities with a positive premium), the timing of turning to align with the price process determines trend following profit.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the convex profile of trend followers, the smile shape
claims.claim: Trend following has a convex payoff versus the market (smile shape), gaining in large moves in either direction.
claims.testable: yes - regress on market and squared market
